regimens.indication: Anticoagulant-Induced Prothrombin Deficiency / VKA (Warfarin) Reversal in Adults

refs.quote: anticoagulant-induced prothrombin deficiency caused by coumarin or indanedione derivatives;

To correct excessively prolonged prothrombin time caused by oral anticoagulant therapy—2.5 to 10 mg or up to 25 mg initially is recommended. In rare instances 50 mg may be required. Frequency and amount of subsequent doses should be determined by prothrombin time response or clinical condition (see WARNINGS).

regimens.dose_text: 2.5 to 10 mg (or up to 25 mg) initially. In severe bleeding or urgent reversal, 5 to 10 mg IV administered by slow infusion (not exceeding 1 mg/min). If prothrombin time has not shortened satisfactorily in 6 to 8 hours, repeat dose.

regimens.indication: Anticoagulant-Induced Prothrombin Deficiency — Adults (Subcutaneous, Preferred Route)

refs.quote: Whenever possible, phytonadione injectable emulsion, should be given by the subcutaneous route. (See Box Warning .)
To correct excessively prolonged prothrombin time caused by oral anticoagulant therapy—2.5 to 10 mg or up to 25 mg initially is recommended. In rare instances 50 mg may be required.

dose.frequency: initial dose (repeat in 6–8 hours if PT not shortened)

regimens.dose_text: 2.5 to 10 mg (or up to 25 mg; rarely 50 mg) SC initially. Subcutaneous route is preferred whenever possible to avoid IV/IM anaphylactoid reactions. Repeat in 6 to 8 hours if prothrombin time has not shortened satisfactorily.

regimens.indication: Prophylaxis of Hemorrhagic Disease of the Newborn (Neonates)

refs.quote: Prophylaxis of Hemorrhagic Diseas e of the Newborn The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that phytonadione be given to the newborn. A single intramuscular dose of phytonadione injectable emulsion 0.5 to 1 mg within one hour of birth is recommended.

dose.frequency: single dose within 1 hour of birth (0.5 to 1 mg)

regimens.dose_text: 0.5 to 1 mg IM as a single dose within 1 hour of birth (use preservative-free diluents if diluted).

regimens.indication: Treatment of Hemorrhagic Disease of the Newborn (Neonates — Subcutaneous)

refs.quote: Phytonadione injectable emulsion 1 mg should be given either subcutaneously or intramuscularly. Higher doses may be necessary if the mother has been receiving oral anticoagulants.

regimens.dose_text: 1 mg SC (higher doses may be necessary if the mother has been receiving oral anticoagulants). Prompt PT shortening in 2 to 4 hours is diagnostic.

regimens.indication: Treatment of Hemorrhagic Disease of the Newborn (Neonates — Intramuscular)

refs.quote: Phytonadione injectable emulsion 1 mg should be given either subcutaneously or intramuscularly. Higher doses may be necessary if the mother has been receiving oral anticoagulants.

regimens.dose_text: 1 mg IM (higher doses may be necessary if the mother has been receiving oral anticoagulants). Prompt PT shortening in 2 to 4 hours is diagnostic.

regimens.indication: Hypoprothrombinemia Due to Antibacterial Therapy, Salicylates, or Malabsorption — Adults

refs.quote: hypoprothrombinemia due to antibacterial therapy; hypoprothrombinemia secondary to factors limiting absorption or synthesis of Vitamin K, e.g., obstructive jaundice, biliary fistula, sprue, ulcerative colitis, celiac disease, intestinal resection, cystic fibrosis of the pancreas, and regional enteritis;

Hypoprothrombinemia Due to Other Causes in Adults A dosage of 2.5 to 25 mg or more (rarely up to 50 mg) is recommended, the amount and route of administration depending upon the severity of the condition and response obtained.

dose.frequency: initial dose (range 2.5 to 25 mg or more; rarely up to 50 mg)

regimens.dose_text: 2.5 to 25 mg or more (rarely up to 50 mg), SC preferred (route and dose depend on severity and response). Consider discontinuing or reducing interfering drugs (e.g., salicylates, antibiotics).

hepatic.value: Phytonadione promotes hepatic synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X. In severe intrinsic liver disease where synthesis is impaired, failure to respond to phytonadione indicates severe hepatic failure.

refs.quote: faulty formation of factors II, VII, IX and X when caused by Vitamin K deficiency or interference with Vitamin K activity.

value: WARNING — INTRAVENOUS AND INTRAMUSCULAR USE: Severe reactions, including fatalities, have occurred during and immediately after INTRAVENOUS injection of phytonadione, even when precautions have been taken to dilute the phytonadione and to avoid rapid infusion. Severe reactions, including fatalities, have also been reported following INTRAMUSCULAR administration. Typically these severe reactions have resembled hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis, including shock and cardiac and/or respiratory arrest.

tier.note: Phytonadione (vitamin K1) is essential physiological replacement therapy safe throughout pregnancy to reverse maternal or neonatal coagulopathy.

refs.quote: Phytonadione (vitamin K1) is preferred and essential to reverse maternal/neonatal coagulopathy (`preferred`); protamine sulfate reverses UFH/LMWH without placental transfer; 4F-PCC and idarucizumab (~48 kDa) are life-saving emergency reversal agents for refractory maternal hemorrhage and should never be withheld in pregnancy (`caution`).

value.management: Use lowest dose of phytonadione required to control bleeding or correct INR; if resuming warfarin, larger doses of anticoagulant or temporary bridging with heparin may be needed.
